_comment: TEMPLATE, not a ready graph. setup-tavus.mjs expands this into a FULL 8-panel chain (4 nodes per panel + 1 lead-in + 1 terminal) every time, regardless of difficulty. Difficulty (0/2/4) is a runtime choice told to the PAL via conversational_context, not a build-time shape — the lead-in node below branches to the right entry point based on that context. Panels before the entry point simply go unreached for that session; the graph still has to define them because it is provisioned once and difficulty varies per session. The graph MUST stay acyclic: Tavus accepts a cyclic graph at POST /v2/objectives and returns 200, but every conversation using it dies ~1s after startup with exception_encountered_during_conversation_startup (verified 2026-07-27, see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md T1 finding 2, decision D16). Do not add allow_loops or an edge back to an earlier panel. Rewritten 2026-07-29 per docs.tavus.io/sections/onboarding-guide/objectives (one objective per distinct outcome, name tool calls explicitly, keep the PAL system prompt from conflicting with the objectives). test/reexplain/retest make the spoken Excalidraw-and-Send instruction unconditionally required every time, with a canvas.question card only ever an optional bonus (never a replacement) when there are 2+ real discrete options. Prefill (0/2/4 worked-example panels) used to be the PAL's own job, live, via a chain of silent tool calls — observed unreliable (anywhere from 0 to 4 of the requested panels actually landing as real tool calls, the rest either never attempted or hallucinated as fake JSON text; see lib/anthropic/prefill.ts). Moved 2026-07-29 to server-side generation before the conversation is even created (app/api/conversation/route.ts's generateAndPersistPrefill) — the lead-in below no longer generates anything, it only branches straight to the correct entry panel, since panels 1..difficulty are already written to Supabase by the time the PAL reads this.

leadIn.objective_prompt: The session context states the difficulty level (0, 2, or 4) — never ask the student for it. If greater than 0, that many panels were already written to the sheet before this session started; say one brief sentence acknowledging that, then move straight into the next panel with the student. If 0, say one brief sentence and move to panel 1. Never regenerate, re-describe, or re-read aloud any panel that is already filled — you did not write them, they already exist.

conditional.panel_1_await: the session context states the difficulty level is 0, or does not state a difficulty level at all
conditional.panel_3_await: the session context states the difficulty level is 2
conditional.panel_5_await: the session context states the difficulty level is 4

panelChain.objective_prompt: Invite the student to write or sketch their own understanding of panel {N} on the Excalidraw canvas. Wait for their notes — they arrive as spoken text. A bare acknowledgment like "yes", "okay", or "let's do it" is not notes — if that is all you receive, ask again for actual content on the canvas and keep waiting; never invent the student's understanding yourself and never move to testing without real notes from them.

Test understanding with a TRANSFER question: pose one small new problem and ask whether and how their concept applies to it. Never ask them to "explain it back". Ask it one of these three ways, chosen by what the answer actually is — for the first two, just ask naturally in speech, there is nothing to call or type, Tavus renders the card for you automatically from how you ask: (1) 2 or more real discrete options — speak the question and the options naturally as part of your sentence; a canvas.question card appears on its own. (2) A short typed answer, no drawing needed — ask for a brief typed answer naturally; a canvas.input text box appears on its own — this is the right choice for most non-multiple-choice questions. (3) The answer genuinely needs a sketch or diagram — only then explicitly tell the student to draw it on the Excalidraw canvas and click "Send notes to Professor Riso". Never ask for typed text via Excalidraw — path (2) is for that. A bare acknowledgment like "yes", "okay", or "sure" is not an answer — it does not count as solid, shaky, or confused; if that is all you receive, ask the question again and keep waiting for real content, never invent an answer on the student's behalf and never call log_understanding_check until you have one. Once you have a real answer, judge it solid, shaky, or confused, and call the log_understanding_check tool for panel {N}, attempt 1 — a real tool call, never written out as text or JSON.

Re-explain panel {N} more simply, from a different angle. Ask the student to answer once more — either revise their notes or answer a new small problem. Same three-way choice as before: discrete options, ask naturally and a canvas.question card appears on its own; short typed answer, ask naturally and a canvas.input box appears on its own; genuine sketch or diagram, explicitly tell them to draw it on Excalidraw and click Send — never Excalidraw for typed text. This is the only re-explanation for this panel. If a slide from the course material would help make this concrete, this is the moment to bring it up.

Test the student's revised understanding with one more small TRANSFER question — different from attempt 1, still never "explain it back". Same three-way choice: discrete options, ask naturally and a canvas.question card appears on its own; short typed answer, ask naturally and a canvas.input box appears on its own; genuine sketch or diagram, explicitly tell them to draw it on Excalidraw and click Send — never Excalidraw for typed text. A bare acknowledgment is still not an answer — if that is all you receive, ask again and keep waiting for real content before judging. Once you have a real answer, judge it solid, shaky, or confused, and call the log_understanding_check tool for panel {N}, attempt 2 — a real tool call, never written out as text or JSON. There is no third attempt regardless of the result.

conditional.gentle_correct: understanding is still shaky or confused after the re-explanation

panelChain.objective_prompt: The student is still confused after one re-explanation and there is no third attempt. Gently tell them the correct understanding of panel {N} in a sentence or two — no dwelling on the miss, warm and direct. A relevant slide here can make the correct explanation concrete instead of just spoken. Then write the panel yourself in clear, correct language and call log_zine_page with panel_number {N}, source "prefill" — this is your explanation, not the student's, so it must never be logged as source "student". If a canvas.question card is currently shown for this panel, immediately call canvas_clear so it disappears. Then move on.

Agree on a light-polish version of the student's own words for panel {N} — recognisably theirs, not your paraphrase — and call log_zine_page with panel_number {N} and source "student". If a canvas.question card is currently shown for this panel, immediately call canvas_clear so it disappears. Then move on.

terminal.objective_prompt: The zine is complete. Give a short recap naming what the student proved and where they fought hardest, for example 'base cases — first try; recursion took two rounds, that's the normal hard part'. Then let them know they can export their zine.
